The following append-ready entries continue numbering from R017 and preserve the unresolved attribution risks.

### New ledger units

#### 2B

- **R026** — Reuters, 5 Nov. 2022, article lines 431–457: Iran acknowledged sending a small number of drones to Russia before the invasion; Ukraine and U.S. officials disputed the timing and scope. Attribution: Iranian state decision, not personally attributed to Khamenei. Contrary evidence: Tehran denied ongoing transfers and said it opposed war. Lenses: `2B.2`, `2B.5`, `2B.8`, `2B.10`. [Source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iran-acknowledges-drone-shipments-to-russia-before-war-kyiv-says-tehran-is-lying-2933668)

- **R027** — U.S. State Department, *Iran 2022 Human Rights Report*, pp. 27–28: documented IRGC-Qods Force support to Syria, Iraq, Yemen, and Russia, including civilian harm from Iranian UAV support. Attribution: government/IRGC level; no personal Khamenei finding. Contrary evidence: report records Iranian claims regarding Kurdish opposition strikes and alleged defensive rationale. Lenses: `2B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.6`, `2B.8`, `2B.10`. [Source](https://www.theadvocatesforhumanrights.org/res/USDOS%2BHuman%2BRights%2BReport%2BIran%2B2022.pdf)

- **R028** — USIP, 19 July 2022, lines 73–85: Khamenei publicly blamed U.S. policy for the Ukraine war while stating Iran favored ending the war. Direct ruler attribution for rhetoric and framing; not evidence of operational restraint. Contrary evidence: Iran abstained on the UN invasion condemnation and voted against Russia’s Human Rights Council suspension. Lenses: `2B.1`, `2B.3`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`. [Source](https://iranprimer.usip.org/blog/2022/mar/03/iran-blames-us-west-ukraine-war)

- **R029** — Khamenei meeting with Qatar’s emir, 12 May 2022: Khamenei said Yemen and Syria could be addressed through regional dialogue without foreign interference. Direct attribution for a stated peace alternative; implementation and proxy compliance are unverified. Contrary evidence: the statement retained a coercive anti-U.S./anti-Israel framing and did not establish civilian-protection measures. Lenses: `2B.3`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`. [Source](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2022/05/12/681971/Iran-Leader-Seyyed-Ali-Khamenei-dialogue-existing-problems-region)

- **R030** — Axios, 27 Apr. 2022, lines 49–72: Iran and Saudi Arabia resumed Baghdad talks focused on normalization and Yemen; Iran expressed support for extending the Yemen truce. Attribution: diplomatic process involving senior Iranian officials, not directly Khamenei. Contrary evidence: Saudi officials sought more practical Iranian action and remained dissatisfied with Iran’s Yemen role. Lenses: `2B.3`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`. [Source](https://www.axios.com/2022/04/27/iran-saudi-arabia-hold-talks)

#### 3B

- **R031** — Amnesty, 12 Apr. 2022, lines 64–106: documented systemic denial or delay of medical care in Iranian prisons, deaths in custody, and failure to conduct independent investigations. Period fit: persistent conditions documented during 2022, with cases extending earlier. Attribution: prison and prosecution authorities; no personal Khamenei finding. Lenses: `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.6`, `3B.9`. [Source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/04/iran-ailing-prisoners-left-to-die-amid-crisis-of-impunity-for-fatal-denial-of-medical-care/)

- **R032** — Amnesty 2022/23 report, lines 69–100: recorded mass arbitrary detention, unfair trials, torture, incommunicado detention, cruel prison conditions, executions, and failures to investigate custody deaths. Attribution: state judiciary and prison apparatus; formal-authority relevance through Khamenei’s appointment power, not personal direction. Lenses: `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`. [Source](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089406.html)

- **R033** — UN Human Rights Council Resolution S-35/1, adopted 24 Nov. 2022, pp. 1–3: documented reported killings, arbitrary detention, sexual violence, torture, internet restrictions, and the need for independent investigation and access. Attribution: resolution records allegations against Iranian authorities, not a personal finding. Lenses: `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`. [Source](https://documents.un.org/doc/undoc/gen/g22/602/10/pdf/g2260210.pdf)

- **R034** — USIP, 21 Oct. 2022, lines 25–57: described killings, beatings, surveillance, internet restrictions, IRGC/Basij mobilization, Khamenei’s framing of protests as enemy-planned, and his distinction between “incited” protesters and others requiring cultural work. Direct attribution for public framing; operational responsibility remains indirect. Contrary evidence: Khamenei and judiciary chief Ejei publicly mentioned dialogue, correction, or differentiated treatment, though later statements demanded harsh sentencing. Lenses: `3B.1`, `3B.3`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`. [Source](https://iranprimer.usip.org/blog/2022/oct/21/irans-response-protests)

- **R035** — Reuters, 1 Oct. 2022, lines 661–687: reported elite disagreement over security tactics during protests; some clerics and politicians urged restraint because greater lethal force could create a point of no return. Contrary institutional evidence: indicates internal resistance or tactical disagreement. Adverse evidence: the same report describes lethal force and repression. Lenses: `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. [Source](https://www.euronews.com/2022/10/01/iran-women-establishment)

#### 4B

- **R036** — Freedom House 2022, lines 82–113: documented regular but noncompetitive elections, Guardian Council candidate disqualification, Khamenei’s appointment powers, and restricted electoral choice. Period fit: 2022 country assessment using the 2021 presidential and earlier parliamentary/Assembly elections as institutional baseline. Lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.5`, `4B.7`.

- **R037** — Freedom House 2022, lines 142–157: documented restricted elected-government authority, Guardian Council veto power, limited but real parliamentary debate, endemic corruption, and weak public accountability. Contrary evidence: legislators sometimes challenged presidents and policies. Lenses: `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [Source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2022)

- **R038** — CFR, 20 Oct. 2022, lines 41–44 and 57–65: described Khamenei’s authority to command armed forces, dismiss officials, countermand legislation, and influence Assembly of Experts selection; also described succession bargaining and possible IRGC involvement. Attribution: formal authority and institutional structure, not proof of a 2022 succession decision. Lenses: `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.10`. [Source](https://www.cfr.org/articles/irans-protesters-want-khamenei-gone-who-iran-s-supreme-leader)

- **R039** — Chatham House, 28 Sept. 2022, lines 417–439: documented constitutional succession rules, temporary leadership arrangements, opaque candidate selection, deep-state bargaining, and Khamenei-office vetting of senior ministers and ambassadors. Period fit: target-period succession analysis; some institutional facts are persistent baseline. Contrary evidence: the formal Assembly of Experts process remains legally relevant even if opaque. Lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [Source](https://www.chathamhouse.org/2022/09/iran-protests-highlight-its-crisis-legitimacy)

- **R040** — Reuters, 1 Oct. 2022, lines 661–689: reported factional disarray, succession maneuvering, and disagreements over how much force to use during protests. Attribution: shared elite governance; does not establish Khamenei’s personal order. Lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.7`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`. [Source](https://www.euronews.com/2022/10/01/iran-women-establishment)

#### 5B

- **R041** — World Bank, *Iran Economic Monitor*, published 3 Aug. 2022, lines 30–39: recorded recovery alongside inflation, fiscal deficits, food-import costs, cash-transfer pressure, climate/water risks, and need for better-targeted social protection. Attribution: national policy environment; not personal Khamenei performance. Lenses: `5B.1`, `5B.2`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/iran/publication/iran-economic-monitor-spring-2022)

- **R042** — IMF Working Paper 2022/181, published 9 Sept. 2022, pp. 1–35, summary: found currency depreciation, fiscal deficits, and sanctions drove inflation; recommended gradual deficit adjustment, inflation targeting, and better-targeted transfers. Attribution: policy analysis, not a personal finding. Lenses: `5B.2`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`. [Source](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/wp/issues/2022/09/09/determinants-of-inflation-in-iran-and-policies-to-curb-it-523280)

- **R043** — USIP, *Iran in 2022: Volatile Economy*: reported Raisi’s 2022 “economic surgery” subsidy/import-FX reform, intended to reduce corruption and fiscal leakage. Attribution: executive policy, not Khamenei personally; implementation and distributional effects require caution. Contrary evidence: the reform had an anti-corruption rationale. Lenses: `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`.

- **R044** — Freedom House 2022, lines 150–157: documented IRGC and bonyad economic influence, weak scrutiny, restricted watchdog capacity, and corruption concerns. Attribution: institutional authority context; no personal-benefit finding. Contrary evidence: anti-corruption prosecutions and official anti-corruption campaigns existed. Lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`. [Source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2022)

- **R045** — PressTV, 30 Sept. 2022: reported official claims that knowledge-based firms had grown to 7,000 active units and over 3% of GDP. Official claim only; no independent verification of jobs, productivity, or distribution. Lenses: `5B.1`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`. [Source](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2022/09/30/690116/Knowledge-based-production)

#### 6B

- **R046** — UNHCR Iran, target-year results, lines 107–130: reported cash assistance reaching 6,722 vulnerable refugee households/26,224 individuals during 2022, using vulnerability assessment and recurrent or one-off transfers. Attribution: UNHCR-led delivery in Iran, not Khamenei attribution. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`, `6B.8`. [Source](https://www.unhcr.org/ir/cash-based-interventions)

- **R047** — World Bank, 3 Aug. 2022, lines 31–39: identified inflationary pressure on lower-income households and called for targeted safety transfers, infrastructure, water management, and tailored institutions. This documents the service and equity problem more than successful government delivery. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/iran/publication/iran-economic-monitor-spring-2022)

- **R048** — 2022 Energy Policy study, DOI `10.1016/j.enpol.2022.113145`: evaluated Iran’s cash-for-subsidy model and found heterogeneous effects by income, geography, energy use, and transfer share. Period fit: publication and analysis in 2022; attribution remains policy-system level. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`.

- **R049** — Minority Rights Group, 2022 briefing: linked the protest crisis to structural ethnic/minority discrimination, economic exclusion, and civil-society repression. Attribution: national institutional pattern, not a personal service-delivery finding. Lenses: `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.7`, `6B.9`. [Source](https://minorityrights.org/resources/protests-discrimination-and-the-future-of-minorities-in-iran/)

- **R050** — UNICEF Iran 2022 country-office reporting: recorded implementation of child health screening in vulnerable areas and coordination with Iran’s Ministry of Education. Attribution: program implementation by UNICEF and ministry partners; no Khamenei-specific credit. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.5`, `6B.8`. [Source](https://www.unicef.org/media/136656/file/Iran-%28Islamic-Republic-of%29-2022-COAR.pdf)

#### 7B

- **R051** — Reuters investigation, persistent institutional evidence: reported that Setad was controlled by Khamenei and that he selected executives and shaped legal protections for its acquisitions, while finding no evidence that he personally enriched himself from its assets. Period fit: inherited institutional condition remaining relevant in 2022; not a target-year transaction. Lenses: `7B.1`, `7B.2`, `7B.4`, `7B.8`. [Source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/conglomerate-controlled-by-iran%27s-supreme-leader-a-winner-from-nuclear-deal-361546)

- **R052** — U.S. State Department 2022 report, Mobarakeh Steel section: recorded a parliamentary investigation alleging approximately $3 billion in corrupt dealings and political ties. Attribution: reported corruption involving officials, not Khamenei personally. Contrary evidence: the investigation itself indicates some institutional scrutiny. Lenses: `7B.2`, `7B.5`, `7B.7`, `7B.10`. [Source](https://www.ecoi.net/de/dokument/2089063.html)

- **R053** — Freedom House 2022, lines 150–157: documented weak oversight of IRGC/bonyad economic actors and restrictions on journalists investigating corruption. Attribution: systemic integrity context; not personal misconduct. Lenses: `7B.3`, `7B.5`, `7B.6`, `7B.9`. [Source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2022)

- **R054** — Tehran Bureau analysis: described tax exemptions, limited auditability, and public-budget exposure of Khamenei-linked institutions. Analytical secondary source; claims require corroboration and must not be converted into personal wealth. Lenses: `7B.2`, `7B.4`, `7B.6`, `7B.8`.

- **R055** — Reuters/Setad contrary finding: the investigation explicitly found no evidence that Khamenei personally tapped Setad assets for enrichment. This is important mitigating evidence against a personal-corruption inference, while leaving institutional accountability unresolved. Lenses: `7B.1`, `7B.7`, `7B.9`. [Source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/conglomerate-controlled-by-iran%27s-supreme-leader-a-winner-from-nuclear-deal-361546)

#### 8B

- **R056** — World Bank, 3 Aug. 2022, lines 30–39: provided measurable macro constraints and policy needs—water management, infrastructure, targeted transfers, jobs, and fiscal management—but no evidence of a ruler-defined portfolio with milestones. Lenses: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/iran/publication/iran-economic-monitor-spring-2022)

- **R057** — USIP 2022 economic analysis: described the subsidy/import-FX reform as a material program intended to reduce corruption and fiscal leakage. Implementation and adaptation evidence remains limited; attribution is primarily to the Raisi government. Lenses: `8B.1`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`, `8B.8`.

- **R058** — PressTV, 30 Sept. 2022: reported growth of knowledge-based companies and a claimed GDP contribution above 3%. This is an official implementation claim without independent monitoring or durable-outcome verification. Lenses: `8B.1`, `8B.3`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`. [Source](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2022/09/30/690116/Knowledge-based-production)

- **R059** — UNICEF Iran 2022 country-office report: recorded a health-screening program for children in vulnerable areas and Ministry of Education coordination. This supports a bounded service-delivery success, but it is UNICEF/ministry implementation rather than Khamenei-attributed execution. Lenses: `8B.3`, `8B.5`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`. [Source](https://www.unicef.org/media/136656/file/Iran-%28Islamic-Republic-of%29-2022-COAR.pdf)

- **R060** — UNHCR Iran, 2022 results, lines 119–130: documents operational targeting, recurrent cash delivery, coordination through the Cash Working Group, and assistance to 6,722 vulnerable households. This is evidence of implemented adaptation/service delivery within Iran, not general ruler effectiveness. Lenses: `8B.3`, `8B.6`, `8B.8`, `8B.9`. [Source](https://www.unhcr.org/ir/cash-based-interventions)

### Disposition change

### Honest shortfall

The continuation improved all eight chapters, but no chapter reached a defensible personal-attribution saturation point. The main unresolved gaps remain:

- direct Khamenei attribution for proxy operations, economic implementation, and welfare delivery;
- command-and-control and crisis-restraint evidence;
- verified personal corruption or enrichment;
- independent monitoring of programs, budgets, milestones, and correction;
- closed-system underreporting and missing domestic records.

No score, score range, ranking, or judge instruction was produced.
